In [[algebra]], '''Quillen's lemma''' states that an [[endomorphism]] of a [[simple module]] over the [[universal enveloping algebra|enveloping algebra]] of a finite-dimensional [[Lie algebra]] over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] ''k'' is algebraic over&nbsp;''k''. In contrast to a version of [[Schur's lemma]] due to Dixmier, it does not require ''k'' to be [[uncountable]].  [[Daniel Quillen|Quillen]]'s original short [[mathematical proof|proof]] uses [[generic flatness]].<!-- indeed, we can just give a proof below. Taku -->
